sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with constitutional jurisprudence and regulatory commercial law framework
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-Spain Reciprocal Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (2007)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (creation of UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006 (AML/CFT obligations); Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUBF); Circular Básica Jurídica of Superintendencia de Sociedades; AML/CFT rules issued by Superintendencia de Sociedades and UIAF.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation of foreign corporate shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or equivalent competent authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; consular legalization if home country is non-Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special Power of Attorney (Poder Especial) for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in principal's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus sworn Spanish translation by authorized translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national ID of each shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, and appointed legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing state civil registry or notarial authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarized copy with sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered office address or virtual office service agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Property owner, managing agent, or licensed virtual office provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Colombia; cross-border documents require apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Interpol notices, EU restrictive measures, and Colombian domestic lists maintained by UIAF and Fiscalía General de la Nación. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to Politically Exposed Persons as defined by Colombian AML/CFT regulations, including review of source of funds and beneficial interest documentation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social – RUES (www.rues.org.co) operated together with the local Cámara de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be presented in a clear Latin-alphabet form; non-Spanish words are permitted provided they are transliterated into Latin characters and do not create confusion with existing registered names. The chosen denomination must not be identical to an existing name in the same or similar economic activity. Accents and special Spanish characters are accepted only in their statutory form and must be registered exactly as cleared.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the same Cámara de Comercio within 10 business days. If the objection is maintained, a formal administrative appeal may be submitted to the Superintendencia de Sociedades within 30 days. A name reservation may be extended only by obtaining a new pre-registration certificate before the initial 30-day validity expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Limited acceptance: a virtual office may be used for correspondence, but the S.A.S. must maintain a physical domicile or serviced office address in Colombia that is accessible for notifications and inspections. A mail-only P.O. Box is not sufficient.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annual probability of unannounced on-site inspection by the Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, or Superintendencia de Sociedades, consistent with standard commercial compliance supervision for low-risk online retail entities.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and homonym certificate (Certificado de Homonimia)
Drafting of bilingual incorporation bylaws and formation documents for S.A.S.
Apostille, notarization, and sworn Spanish translation of foreign shareholder and UBO documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notary tariff and translation market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: S.A.S. registration proced fee in RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff for limited liability entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Ultimate beneficial owner (RUBF) initial filing through RUES
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Superintendencia de Sociedades / Cámara de Comercio
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory fee; absorbed in registration formality

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office address service for first quarter (serviced office/virtual office support)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-31, especially Article 5 on capital and Article 22 on representation; Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971) Articles 110-111 and 373 et seq.; Decree 1074 of 2015 as codifying the RUES regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office jurisdiction, for example Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, filing via Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) and producing the RUES record.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) executed by shareholders and filed with the Chamber of Commerce; public deed (escritura pública) required if assets contributing require transfer by public instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies. A Colombian S.A.S. may be incorporated with zero paid-up capital, and subscribed capital may be paid in installments under a maximum two-year term if the bylaws provide for it. No escrow account or capital blockage is required for online retail activities.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The incorporator, acting as sole shareholder, adopts the signed private incorporation document and bylaws and subscribes 100 nominative ordinary shares of [Company] S.A.S. The registered office shall be [exact address in Colombia], Municipality [City]. The authorized capital may remain unpaid; the company confirms no minimum capital requirement under Law 1258 of 2008. The Board appoints [Name] as Legal Representative/General Manager and [Name] as alternate officer, with powers to open bank accounts, complete DIAN tax registration, issue invoices, administer the e-commerce platform, and request municipal permits. The Board ratifies all acts and decisions taken in accordance with this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name availability and similarity check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comerco of the intended registered office; online service through Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE, www.vue.gov.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic name search for the S.A.S. requesting at least three preferred denominations. The Chamber verifies the proposed names against the national merchant registry and issues a name availability certificate. The application must be made before any incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Identification document or passport of each incorporator
Power of attorney if the filing is done by an intermediary
List of three preferred corporate names in requested order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar to an existing registration, obtain the formal rejection notice and submit a new availability request using materially different wording or adding a distinguishing sign.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the incorporation instrument and bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private shareholders meeting; notary public only when a public deed is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución containing corporate name, domicile, corporate purpose (online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets), capital structure, share subscription, board and officer provisions, and audit arrangements. All shareholders sign, with identity authenticated before a public notary when prudent. If real or registered assets are contributed, execute a public escritura before a notary.
required_dossiers: Approved corporate bylaws (estatutos) with Law 1258 mandatory clauses
National IDs or passports of all shareholders
Lease or proof of address for the registered office in Colombia
Inventory and appraisals for in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or shareholder review rejects the draft for missing legal clauses, correct the bylaws, re-sign all pages, and resubmit; no judicial remedy is required because the correction is administrative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Merchant registration with the Chamber of Commerce and RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered office city through RUES
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After execution, file the signed incorporation instrument, name availability certificate, and the completed RUES form at the Chamber. Pay the registration fee. The Chamber verifies the filing, records the company, issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, and assigns a provisional NIT for later definitive DIAN registration.
required_dossiers: Executed private incorporation instrument or public deed
Name availability certificate
Completed RUES application form
Proof of payment of Chamber registration fees
Identification documents of the legal representative and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a query or clarification notice, correct the indicated fields in the RUES database, pay any adjusted tariff, and resubmit within five business days; legal representation may be fixed by an amended board resolution and supplementary filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and electronic invoicing setup with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) through MUISCA online system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Chamber-issued company certificate, obtain the definitive RUT (Registro Único Tributario) and NIT. Select the applicable income tax regime for commercial companies, configure electronic invoicing authorization, attach the legal representative's digital signature, and activate the invoice emission profile for retail operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and existence from the Chamber of Commerce
Provisional NIT or RUT application number
Identity document of the legal representative
Confirmed fiscal address in Colombia
Digital certificate issued by an authorized certification entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN queries the application due to address mismatch or incomplete ISIC activities, update the RUT using MUISCA online services and resubmit supporting utility or lease documents; a face-to-face appointment at the nearest DIAN office may be requested.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance implementation and opening of the corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / legal representative and the chosen Colombian commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting, record the pro-forma resolution in the corporate minute book, and certify the appointment of officers. Open the company bank account at a regulated bank, present the certified existence certificate, governance documents, and KYC information. If paid-in capital has been contributed, deposit it; if zero capital was elected, record the capital structure as subscribed and unpaid.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
First board resolution and appointment of legal representative
Bylaws filed with the Chamber
Identification and background records of shareholders and beneficial owners
Bank KYC forms and expected transaction profile for online retail card payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional beneficial ownership disclosure, provide an organizational chart, the shareholders' register, and supporting identification; if the corporate minute book has not been stamped by the Chamber, register it before reopening the account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal, physical, and e-commerce operational compliance check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal planning authority; fire department; Ministry of Labor/ARL; Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) for consumer e-commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the registered office or warehouse complies with local land-use rules (uso del suelo). If a physical warehouse is operated, obtain the municipal land-use certificate and fire-safety certificate. Register employees with an ARL and enact the occupational health and safety plan. For online retail, publish the required consumer information, privacy policy, and e-commerce terms in accordance with Colombian consumer protection rules; no industrial operating license is required for ISIC 4791 retail operations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Lease agreement or property title for the registered physical location
Land-use compatibility certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo)
Fire-safety inspection certificate from Cuerpo de Bomberos
ARL affiliation certificate and workplace safety plan
Published e-commerce privacy and consumer contract documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the use-of-soil authorization is denied, relocate the registered office or warehouse to a permitted commercial zone and file a new certificate; if fire-safety inspection identifies deficiencies, remedy the physical conditions, request reinspection, and retain the compliance certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial sectoral license authority is triggered for pure online retail of consumer electronics; the municipal planning office and the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio regulate land use and e-commerce commerce compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no separate operating or manufacturing permit is required for ISIC 4791 online retail of personal electronics and smart gadgets.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category IV administrative compliance; no full or preliminary environmental impact assessment is required for a low-impact e-commerce retail and warehousing operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOCs are generated by online retail activity. Applicable obligations are limited to municipal solid-waste separation and compliance with Resolution 6982 of 2011 on the management of e-waste (RAEE) if electronics are imported, distributed, or returned.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical office or warehouse, the company must obtain the Cuerpo de Bomberos fire-safety certificate, the municipal land-use certificate, and an ARL occupational health and safety affiliation. Structural load inspections are only mandatory for unusually high-density warehousing; ordinary low-load retail e-commerce storage falls under general commercial building clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — Colombia's national tax and customs authority. Official portal: www.dian.gov.co. All registrations, electronic filings, RUT updates, and invoice clearances are processed through DIAN's centralized e-services platform 'MUISCA' (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) and the 'Sede Electrónica' using a digital certificate (certificado digital) issued by an authorized certification authority. Customs and export declarations are submitted through DIAN's 'Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior' (VUCE) and the 'Declaración de Exportación' gateway.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A.S. (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada) via private document (documento privado) before the Cámara de Comercio of the registered domicile; obtain the certificado de existencia y representación legal; no minimum capital is required and 100% non-resident ownership is permitted. Step 2: Appoint a legal representative with Colombian nationality or residency, or grant a power of attorney (poder legalizado/apostillado and translated into Spanish by an authorized traductor oficial) to a local agent; register the foreign shareholder's identification with the chamber. Step 3: Submit the 'Pre-RUT' application electronically through DIAN's 'RUT Virtual' portal (www.dian.gov.co), declaring the S.A.S.'s commercial activity (ISIC 4791), registered address, establishment details, and the electronic invoicing contact; the foreign shareholder must provide apostilled incorporation documents, bylaws, and a local fiscal domicile address. Step 4: DIAN performs the 'validación previa' and assigns the definitive NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) including the two-digit verification digit (DV) — the mandatory tax identifier for all filings, invoices, and customs declarations. Step 5: Finalize registration by biometric validation/electronic signature of the legal representative or authorized proxy; the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) is then issued with the status 'Responsable del régimen común de IVA' and 'Declarante de renta'. Step 6: Within the same process, activate the mandatory facturación electrónica system in MUISCA and register the taxpayer as an 'habilitado para facturar electrónicamente', appointing a certified proveedor tecnológico (PT) or using DIAN's free invoicing tool; a revisor fiscal must be appointed where statutory thresholds (gross assets > 5,000 UVT or gross income > 5,000 UVT) are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (full corporate taxpayer — 'Régimen Ordinario del Impuesto sobre la Renta'). Under Articles 12 et seq. of the Estatuto Tributario, the Colombian-resident S.A.S. is a separate juridical person taxed on worldwide income at 35% for tax year 2025 (Law 2277 of 2022 preserves the 35% rate). The entity is classified as 'Gran Contribuyente' or ordinary taxpayer in the RUT, is an 'Responsable del IVA' in the common regime without pass-through eligibility, and is subject to dividend withholding at source on distributions to non-resident shareholders (generally a 10% surcharge on distributions from profits taxed at the corporate level), plus the applicable municipal industry and commerce tax (ICA). Territorial-source rules apply only to non-resident entities; the S.A.S., being a resident company, is subject to entity-level taxation on its Colombian and foreign-sourced income. No check-the-box pass-through transparency is available for a Colombian S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Colombian law for an S.A.S.; the entity is irrebuttably treated as a corporation for income tax and IVA purposes. Available elective regimes: (1) Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLES) — an optional presumptive/combined income-tax-plus-IVA regime under Law 1943 of 2018 and Law 2010 of 2019, available only when annual gross turnover does not exceed 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4.98 billion in 2025) and other activity-specific thresholds are satisfied; retail e-commerce operators may opt into SIMPLES but the full turnover of a major consumer-electronics retailer generally disqualifies it. (2) Régimen ZESE (Zonas Económicas y Sociales Especiales) — a 20% income tax rate election for new companies established in qualifying underdeveloped municipalities; not applicable to a main establishment in a major city such as Bogotá. (3) Régimen de Compañías Holding Colombianas (CHC) under Law 2010 of 2019 — electable by a Colombian S.A.S. that holds shares in foreign entities, providing territorial exemption for dividends from abroad, capital gains on foreign share disposals, and reduced withholding on outbound interest/dividends; requires a minimum qualified shareholding, substantial domestic substance, and formal election in the annual tax return. (4) Hybrid mismatch limitations: Colombia has enacted OECD-compliant hybrid instrument and hybrid entity rules in Decree 1625 of 2016 and Law 2277 of 2022; a resident S.A.S. participating in cross-border structures must document that no double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcome arises. (5) Fiscal consolidation is not permitted; each S.A.S. files on a stand-alone basis.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre las Ventas (Value Added Tax of the European-style structure, levied at each stage of the commercial cycle with full credit mechanism for inputs).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de-minimis threshold for legal entities: a Colombian S.A.S. selling taxable consumer-electronics goods is a mandatory 'Responsable del IVA' in the 'régimen común' from the first peso of taxable turnover, and must obtain the RUT/VAT registration before commencing sales. A simplified taxpayer regime ('régimen simplificado') is restricted to individual natural persons with annual gross sales not exceeding 3,500 UVT (COP 174,296,500 for 2025, using UVT 2025 = COP 49,799) and only where other conditions are met — this status is not available to the S.A.S. corporate entity. Foreign digital service providers selling into Colombia also require VAT registration without any low-turnover exemption. Optionally, an S.A.S. under the SIMPLES regime is liable for a combined monthly payment that includes an IVA component, but the standard 19% statutory rate applies to each taxable transaction of the retail activity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory full electronic invoicing ('Factura Electrónica de Venta' or FEV) applies to all Colombian IVA-responsible taxpayers, fully enforced since 2022 under DIAN Resolution 000165 of 2023 and related technical standards. The S.A.S. must transmit each sales invoice in XML/UBL 2.1 format over SOAP/REST web services to DIAN's MUISCA platform through a certified 'proveedor tecnológico' or through DIAN's free electronic invoicing portal; DIAN performs real-time pre-validation ('validación previa') and returns a CDR (acuse de recibo) with an assigned unique CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica). A digital stamp in the form of a QR code containing the CUFE and the DIAN validation URL must be embedded on every printed or PDF invoice; continuous contingency ('contingencia electrónica') procedures apply during platform outages, using CUDS/CUDE codes, with the mandatory transmission of the contingency batch once connectivity is restored. The invoice catalogue includes, among others, the standard sale invoice, the 'documento soporte en adquisiciones a sujetos no obligados a facturar', and the electronic export invoice; e-commerce payment gateways such as Stripe and PayPal do not substitute for the DIAN-validated local FEV, and the S.A.S. remains solely responsible for the issuance and clearance of the invoice to the end consumer.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and qualifying exports of services are 'excluidos' of IVA at 0% under Article 481 and following of the Estatuto Tributario, implemented through Decree 1625 of 2016 (Article 1.3.1.4.2.1 onwards). The S.A.S. retailer may zero-rate a consumer-electronics sale where: (i) the goods are physically delivered out of Colombia to a final buyer abroad, evidenced by a customs export declaration accepted by DIAN; (ii) the sale is made to a foreign buyer (with no Colombian intermediary or final in-country delivery); (iii) the payment is received through a Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary ('intermediario del mercado cambiario'); and (iv) the export proceeds are repatriated within the mandatory 180-day term. For digitally-delivered services or software incorporated in smart gadgets, the 'export services' zero-rating additionally requires that the benefit is exclusively exploited abroad and that the exporter holds the documentary evidence required by Article 1.3.1.4.2.3 of Decree 1625/2016. The zero-rated export VAT position enables the S.A.S. to claim refunds of input VAT (IVA descontable) attributable to the exported goods through the 'solicitud de devolución' procedure (Form 350) before DIAN, with a mandatory refund period that DIAN represerves for payment after the automatic 15-day and then, however, in practice, is issued within an approximate 30- to 90-day administrative timeline.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación — Form 620/DEX) accepted and validated by DIAN customs through the VUCE/export gateway, evidencing final exit of the goods
Bill of Lading (maritime or cross-border trucking bill) or Air Waybill revealing shipment from Colombia to the foreign buyer's address and destination

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa de Fondos) issued by the Colombian foreign-exchange intermediary, evidencing repatriation of proceeds in hard currency against the export documents
Accompanying commercial invoice, purchase order, and sales contract reflecting the agreed INCOTERMS, export price, and the foreign buyer's identity
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN audits zero-rated exporters using cross-matched databases that reconcile the Declaración de Exportación, the shipping manifests, the bank foreign-exchange reports, and the VAT refund claims. Any discrepancy may void the zero-rating and result in a recharacterization of the export as a taxable domestic sale. Clawback and penalty consequences include: (i) collection of 19% VAT on the full export value where zero-rating documentation is defective, plus daily default interest (computed at the current monthly interest rate, historically in the 1.7%–2.9% band); (ii) the 'sanción por devoluciones y compensaciones improcedentes' of 20% of the VAT refund improperly obtained or claimed (Article 670 Estatuto Tributario); (iii) the 'sanción por inexactitud' of 100% of the higher tax due, escalated to 160% where the misstatement is considered aggravated under Law 2277 of 2022; (iv) exchange-control sanctions for failure to repatriate within 180 days or for channeling proceeds outside the official foreign-exchange market, which may reach up to 200% of the non-repatriated amount under the Colombian exchange-control rules (Estatuto Cambiario and Resolution 8 of 2000); and (v) criminal exposure for tax fraud under Article 402 of the Código Penal when fraudulent documentation (simulated export declarations, false bills of lading, or forged remittance certificates) is utilized, carrying custodial penalties of up to ten years. The full supporting documentation must be retained for the statutory limitation period of the relevant tax returns, which extends up to ten years in cases of fraud, and the burden of proving the zero-rating requirements lies with the exporter.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), jointly administering the Estatuto Cambiario with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (SFC) as supervisor of foreign-exchange-licensed intermediaries and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) as customs and enforcement authority; the normative base is Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1735 of 1993, and Resolución Externa 1 of 2021 (as amended), which consolidates all foreign-exchange (cambiario) regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is a freely floating currency with unrestricted convertibility for current-account transactions and a broadly open capital account subject to mandatory channeling through the Mercado Cambiario (MCR) via SFC-authorized intermediaries. Foreign direct investment (FDI) into a Colombian SAS must be registered with Banco de la República through the local receiving bank (via the FIC/SIE electronic declaration system) under concept code 4010 for equity capital. Profit and dividend remittances are permitted without separate exchange-control authorization provided that (i) the foreign investor's equity interest is duly registered, (ii) the entity has filed and paid its corporate income tax obligations, (iii) the applicable dividend withholding tax regime has been honored (generally 5% on profits previously taxed at 35% and up to 10% in preferential cases), and (iv) the outgoing transfer is declared under the correct dividend-channeling concept code. Practical remittance hurdles for a SAS with non-resident owners include DIAN insistence on updated RUT/NIT documentation for the foreign investor, SFC-mandated UBO disclosure, and the local bank's policy requiring audited financial statements before any profit distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of physical goods must bring 100% of export proceeds into Colombia through the Mercado Cambiario within six months from the date of shipment (Bill of Lading or airway bill). Foreign-exchange proceeds are deemed 'chanelled' when either (a) converted into COP through an SFC-licensed bank with submission of the Formulario de Información Cambiaria (FIC), or (b) deposited into a declared foreign-currency account (cuenta corriente en moneda extranjera) held with a local bank; no mandatory conversion into COP is required if the company keeps and uses the foreign-currency balance for authorized outflows such as imports, foreign-debt service, or re-export settlements. For e-commerce transactions settled in COP by Stripe or PayPal through a Colombian licensed acquirer, the underlying export declaration (DEX) must reconcile with the PSP batch reports and no separate FX surrender is triggered because the proceeds are already routed through the local settlement system; however, any sales proceeds accumulated abroad in USD/EUR through foreign PSP balances must be repatriated into the MCR within the same six-month statutory window for goods exports. Services-related digital sales, including software and digital value-added services, benefit from a five-year channeling window from the service accrual date under Resolución Externa 1 of 2021, but the same 100% channeling obligation applies to all export revenue regardless of the receiving rail.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI/channeling USD foreign-currency account) + Operational COP Current Account
Capital Escrow Account (foreign-currency inflow account) + Operational COP Account with full trade-services desk
Capital Escrow Account (foreign-currency account) + Operational COP Account with ACH Colombia PSP payout clearing
Capital Escrow Account + Operational COP Account with USD/COP forward and derivative access via BBVA Group
Capital Escrow Account (USD settlement account) + Operational COP Account with Scotiabank North American trade corridor
Capital Escrow Account (foreign-currency account) + Operational COP Account with FDI registration and external credit support
Capital Escrow Account + Operational COP Account with import letter-of-credit facilities
Operational COP Account only; limited foreign-currency services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-TO-MEDIUM with material legal constraints. Stripe (through local licensed acquirer partners such as CredibanCo/Bambú) and PayPal (with local bank settlement to a Colombian account) are permissible PSP collection rails that settle in COP and reconcile with the Estatuto Cambiario. However, a Colombian SAS cannot lawfully treat an offshore EMI balance (Wise Business, Airwallex, Mercury, Dukascopy, Revolut Business) as a treasury settlement account: the FX regime obliges exporters to channel all proceeds through the MCR via SFC-licensed banks; leaving collected funds in an unlicensed foreign EMI breaches the channeling obligation and exposes the entity to cambiario sanctions (fines up to 200% of the transaction value imposed by SFC/DIAN), complicates import-payment substantiation, and triggers enhanced AML classification at the local bank. The compliant structure is: PSP collection in COP through local acquiring settlement; any foreign EMI usage limited to minor operational expenses and always repatriated/declared within the statutory timeline.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a SAS owned by non-resident shareholders with a local legal representative, the legal representative (or a duly appointed attorney-in-fact holding a Colombian-issued legal ID) must appear physically at a commercial banking branch for the initial KYC interview; fully remote video onboarding is not universally accepted for corporate entities with foreign UBOs. A minority of Tier-1 banks (Bancolombia, Davivienda) offer hybrid digital onboarding for wholly domestically owned small entities using biometric e-KYC, but any foreign shareholder automatically triggers added due diligence, apostilled powers of attorney, certified passport copies, and board minutes appointing the local signatory. The practical mandate is at least one physical visit by the legal representative to sign the account contract, followed by periodic AML refreshes; non-resident directors may otherwise act under a power of attorney without further personal appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owner lacks a Colombian tax ID (NIT) and cannot fully evidence source of wealth to the bank's Sarlaft unit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn UBO declaration per SFC Circular Básica Jurídica formats, passport with certified translation, bank reference letters from the home institution issued within 90 days, source-of-wealth report with business ownership track record, and applicable DIAN registration data for the foreign investor under the RUT system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce refund and chargeback ratio with high transaction velocity triggering PSP risk modeling for consumer electronics retail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of Stripe/PayPal settlement reports, refund and dispute ratio attestation (target below 0.9% Visa and below 1.2% Mastercard thresholds), store return policy and logistics tracking evidence, AVS/CVV usage confirmation, chargeback representment workflow documentation, and a copy of the merchant agreement with the Colombian acquiring partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between registered business activity (online retail) and observed large USD-denominated inward flows from overseas cardholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cámara de Comercio certificate issued within 30 days stating ISIC 4791 activity, active store URL and platform details, commercial supplier contracts with China/US distributors, customs export declarations (DEX) evidencing each physical exit, PSP transaction reconciliation, and a management letter describing the fulfilment chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward capital contribution arriving from a related offshore company or a high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate ownership chart, audited financials of the originator, SWIFT reference details, the foreign-investment registration filed with Banco de la República through the receiving local bank, mandate confirming FDI concept code 4010, no-encumbrance certificate for the originating funds, and AML/TF screening evidence against OFAC/EU/UN sanction lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recently incorporated SAS with no operating history and minimal declared capital (Colombian law imposes no minimum capital)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RUT/NIT and Cámara de Comercio certificate, detailed business plan with revenue projections, execution of a declared capitalization consistent with sales expectations, board resolution accepting bank contracts and designated signatories, personal guarantee or side-letter of the same legal representative where requested, and up to three months of preliminary PSP transaction history where available.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholder equity is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's upstream bank to the Colombian bank's USD correspondent (nostro), referencing the beneficiary SAS's foreign-currency or peso account. The receiving bank verifies the UBO against sanction lists, credits the company's USD capital-import account, and converts to COP at the market reference rate (TCR) upon presentation of the Cambiario declaration; the bank then files the FDI registration with Banco de la República under concept code 4010 within the statutory deadline. For shareholder loans classified as external credit, the drawdown must be registered under the external-loan concept code and the entity remains subject to quarterly information declarations. The complete routing documentation set comprises: the MT103 confirmation, the signed bank-internal foreign-investment declaration, the Cámara de Comercio certificate, the NIT/RUT, a certified passport copy of the foreign investor, and the board resolution approving the capital increase and account signatories. All funds must be reflected in the investment registration before the SAS distributes dividends or repays equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Import and supplier payments for consumer electronics procured from China, the United States, and regional warehouses settle through: (i) SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers denominated in USD/EUR/CNY via the local bank's FX desk, with the import customs declaration (Declaración de Importación) referenced to substantiate the payment; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by the Colombian bank and advised through the supplier's confirming bank for large recurring procurement loads; and (iii) direct USD debits from the declared foreign-currency account when accumulated export balances are applied. PSP payouts from Stripe and PayPal settle in COP through the local acquiring network (ACH Colombia / Cámara de Compensación) into the company's operational current account, eliminating FX conversion on the collection side. Disbursements for cross-border platform fees, cloud subscriptions, overseas advertising, and digital services are payable via SWIFT MT103 with the correct import-of-services or royalty concept code, supported by commercial invoices and applicable DIAN withholding-tax certificates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/COP forward contracts (contratos forward) offered by authorized local banks, requiring evidence of underlying commercial exposure from import/export flows and internal board delegation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the USD/COP rate, permitted for local entities hedging real exposures without physical delivery, executed through an SFC-authorized intermediary or a recognized offshore bank in mirror with the local bank's hedge transaction.
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD and occasionally EUR/COP) used to match foreign-currency assets and liabilities or to convert variable-rate foreign debt into local-currency obligations.
Vanilla FX options on USD/COP purchased to cap the entity's maximum import cost or to protect export margins; option-writing is restricted for non-financial corporate entities.

Exchange-traded USD/COP futures and options quoted on recognized international venues (such as CME) and executed through a local broker, permissible for micro-hedging of high-frequency e-commerce settlement flows subject to the company's documented derivative policy and real-exposure test.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil (annual renewal of commercial registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 – March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of 5% of the applicable renewal fee per month or fraction; two consecutive years without renewal triggers cancellation of the registry; the entity cannot operate formally and faces administrative fines up to 10 SMMLV.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (annual corporate income tax return, Form 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually for the calendar tax year; staggered NIT-based due dates published by DIAN, generally between April and June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax owing per month or fraction, capped at 100% of the tax; minimum penalty of approximately 1,000 UVT when no tax is payable; default interest accrues from the original due date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Declaración Anual de Beneficiarios Finales (annual UBO information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Regulatory regime: Resolución 164 de 2023 and subsequent updates)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the NIT-staggered calendar published by DIAN, in practice between May and July of the year following the reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of up to COP 25,000,000 (approx. USD 6,300) per infraction for failure to file, late filing, or submitting inaccurate final beneficial owner information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Aprobación de Estados Financieros y Acta de Asamblea (annual shareholders' meeting and filing of approved statutory financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (financial statements must be filed together with the commercial registry renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must be held no later than March 31 of the following fiscal year (within three months after the closing of the annual accounts).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-approval or non-filing prevents the annual renewal of the commercial registration; legal representatives and the public accountant are jointly liable for damages and may face administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Información Exógena Anual (annual third-party transaction report to DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year on the NIT-based due date announced by DIAN, generally between June and July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sanction under Article 651 of the Colombian Tax Code up to 24,324 UVT (approx. COP 1.21 billion / USD 300,000) for refusal to supply, material inaccuracy, or undue delay; voluntary correction before notification reduces the sanction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory for a SAS when total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.6 million in 2025) or gross income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.0 million in 2025) in the immediately preceding fiscal year. Mandatory also for issuers of public securities, public-interest entities, and certain concessionaires. Below the thresholds, independent audit is optional and financial statements may be prepared and certified by the entity's ordinary Contador Público.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Law 1314 de 2009: full International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) for listed and public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs (NIIF para PYMES) for the standard SAS e-commerce retailer not issuing public securities. Books and supporting records must be preserved for a minimum of ten years (Código de Comercio Art. 58).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SAS must file an annual declaration with DIAN identifying every final beneficial owner (natural person) with direct or indirect ownership, control, or benefit equal to or greater than 5%. The declaration must be submitted every year within the NIT-based DIAN window, even if there has been no shareholding transfer during the period. On any transfer of shares, the shareholders' register must be updated immediately and the annual declaration compliantly revised to reflect the new ultimate beneficiary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Libro de Registro de Accionistas (Register of Shareholders)
Libro de Actas de la Asamblea (Shareholders' meeting minutes book)
Libro de Actas de la Junta Directiva (Board minutes book, when a board has been constituted)
Libro Diario and Libro Mayor (accounting books duly registered with DIAN)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – USD 750 per year for a compliant registered office/administrative address in a major city; no registered agent is required for a Colombian SAS
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 – USD 15,000 per year for a certified statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) depending on asset level, transaction volume, and IFRS reporting complexity; USD 800 – USD 1,500 for a reviewed financial statement prepared by a public accountant when below the audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (standard corporate income tax rate for FY2024; Law 2277 of 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holidays for e-commerce retail. Deductions available include: (i) 100% of investments in scientific research, technological development and innovation (over 6 years? no) ...
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (unlimited carryforward under E.T. Art. 147, as amended by Law 1819/2016); annual offset limited to 50% of taxable income for FY2023 and 30% for FY2025 onwards (Law 2277/2022)
